# Pass Two — Gevurah Critique and Improvements

The Awtsmoos gives boundless light, yet vessels make the light precise;
this pass restrains the dream to changes that can be tested twice.

## Critique of pass one
- A single renderer for every app would erase legitimate differences; share contracts and timing, not necessarily every pixel path.
- “Any movie” cannot mean unrestricted arbitrary JavaScript from AI. It must mean a broad, validated declarative movie language with extensible commands.
- 3D characters may not have full rigged animation assets available locally; fallback procedural people must still prove actor/camera/staging capability.
- Audio synthesis is not guaranteed. The core should support audio cues and narration timing without falsely claiming speech generation.
- Exporting encoded MP4 may depend on browser/runtime capabilities. A deterministic 180-second playable movie is mandatory; encoded export is secondary unless already supported.
- Existing applications may contain mature engines worth adapting instead of replacing.
- Concurrent work means every target file must be re-read immediately before rewrite and public contracts preserved.

## Thirty concrete improvements
1. Discover all movie surfaces with filename/content search, not app-name guesses.
2. Trace entry HTML, module imports, and runtime boot for each candidate.
3. Record current public APIs before changes.
4. Separate canonical schema from renderers.
5. Use stable IDs for scenes, tracks, actors, cameras, and objects.
6. Make duration numeric and clamp negative/NaN values.
7. Derive total duration from scenes when absent.
8. Add scene-local time evaluation.
9. Add absolute timeline time evaluation.
10. Add declarative keyframes.
11. Add motion presets as sugar over keyframes.
12. Add easing utilities shared by 2D/3D.
13. Add 2D primitives required for charts/tutorials.
14. Add 3D primitives required for cinematic geometry.
15. Add particle emitters in both 2D and 3D adapters where practical.
16. Add text/typewriter/count-up behavior.
17. Add actor primitives with reusable IDs.
18. Add named cameras and camera cuts.
19. Add camera motion presets.
20. Add scene transition metadata with graceful fallback.
21. Add schema validation messages suitable for AI repair loops.
22. Add a compiler from structured AI program instructions to canonical movie data.
23. Add persona presets rather than duplicating engine logic.
24. Add mobile viewport rules and large touch targets.
25. Make preview resize with `ResizeObserver` or a proven existing equivalent.
26. Ensure timeline scrub works by touch/pointer events.
27. Make the showcase data-driven, not embedded in renderer code.
28. Assert showcase duration is 180 seconds within numeric tolerance.
29. Test multiple scene boundaries and object types programmatically.
30. Browser-test at desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
31. Check console errors after route load and after playback/scene seeks.
32. Re-read every written file and run tab/line-length style audits.
33. Compare planned vs actual touched files.
34. Keep a final `REMAINING_WORK` ledger until every required item is evidence-backed.
35. Document known limitations honestly rather than hiding them.

## Realistic architecture target
- Reuse the strongest existing movie core if repository evidence reveals one.
- Otherwise create `apps/shared/movie/` with small modules for model, validation, time/easing, compiler, 2D primitives, 3D primitives, playback controller, and persona presets.
- Integrate candidate apps through thin adapters/imports instead of cloning the shared core.
- Preserve each app’s visual shell and default workflow while exposing the same underlying project vocabulary.

## Verification target
- Node/static syntax checks for all touched JS.
- Focused unit-like scripts for validation/timeline/compiler.
- Existing tests relevant to each app.
- Browser route loads with console inspection.
- Mobile viewport interaction checks.
- Showcase seek checks at 0s, scene boundaries, midpoint, and near 180s.
